speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether he can provide an update on how many Autonomous Vehicles (AV) have passed Milestone 1 and 2 tests respectively; and (b) whether AV development in Singapore is progressing as planned, particularly for autonomous public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: AV companies would, therefore, have to undertake further research and development and trials.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I first declare my interest as the executive secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU).

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think, globally, we have started seeing commercial trials of AVs ferrying passengers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, there remains significant concerns over safety risks, especially in high-density environments, such as that in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As the Government reviews its AV plans, will the Ministry consider a deliberate slowing down of our deployment timelines, especially for our public transport, until such time when the technology is more mature and safer?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I would also like to ask if the Ministry can work closely with the unions to prepare and transit our workers in the public transport sector, such as bus captains, taxi drivers, private hire vehicle drivers, in line with the AV deployment timeline.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think we should provide our unions and our workers sufficient time to adjust and to adapt to a driverless world.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, of course, is the progress of the AV technology and, importantly, to be able to meet safety standards and operational requirements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And then, finally, there is public acceptance, which is also very important in order for larger-scale deployment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will let the technology and the commercial viability, and also, the awareness and public acceptance, make progress steadily.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But if we are able to have some breakthroughs, I think that will be beneficial.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With regard to the collaborations on preparing our workers for this transition, I think that is an extremely important area.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Allow me, Mr Speaker, just to share briefly.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The roadmap will identify emerging skills and what are some of the new job roles arising from the deployment of autonomous technologies, and what are the courses and on-the-job training that we can provide to our workers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: LTA will also work closely with industry players and with SkillsFuture Singapore to update the existing skills framework to ensure relevance for the bus workforce.
